subject: Re: MAP + performance runbook and access (DataCo)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@dataco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: MAP + performance runbook and access (DataCo)

Dana — attaching the MAP draft and our proposed benchmarking runbook for the close. High-level asks:

- Goal: validate production-grade throughput and latency for your core inference path (batch size 1 & 4). Demonstrate TTFT under cold and warm cache conditions, and steady-state concurrency targets.
- Success criteria: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 450ms, steady throughput >= 1800 RPS at 256 token median, TTFT under 120ms for hot-cache requests; no more than one 2-minute service disruption during steady-state windows.
- Mutual actions: we need test credentials + access to the staging ingress, an account with the same model weights you’ll serve in prod, and a small seeded workload that mirrors your traffic profile. See MAP tab "Milestones" in attached DataCo_MAP_v1.xlsx.
- Logistics: proposed load windows (UTC): Sep 15 22:00–00:00 (steady-state + spike tests), Sep 16 02:00–03:30 (long-run). Please confirm which window works for your infra team.

Attachments: DataCo_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + runbook).

Next step: Dana, can you confirm access and drop the test credentials (or a secure link) here by EOD Sep 11? Laura — can you own the collector configuration and ingestion of metrics? Aditya — we'll need you on the orchestration pair for the spike tests.

Thanks,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@dataco.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataCo Performance Team <perf@dataco.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 14:03:22 +0000
Subject: Re: MAP + performance runbook and access (DataCo)

Thanks Karthik — plan looks good. We can provide staging ingress and a test account. Quick notes/asks:

- Credentials: attached dataco-test-credentials.txt (API key stub + endpoint). We will follow up with a short-lived KMS token for any HSM-protected keys.
- Model parity: you'll have access to the exact model snapshot we plan to push to production on 09/20; the snapshot tag is prod-20260901.
- TTFT measurement: confirm you will measure TTFT from request-accept to first-token-out (not end-of-generation). Also clarify warm-cache protocol: we expect a 5-minute warmup to reach steady-state; please include a separate cold-run (no cache priming).
- We agree to Sep 15 22:00–00:00 UTC for the controlled window. Perf team will monitor.

Attachments: dataco-test-credentials.txt

Dana Lopez
Director, Site Reliability — DataCo
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MAP + performance runbook and access (DataCo)

Laura / Aditya — confirming our internal plan before the SEP15 window. Runbook excerpt:

- 21:30 UTC: pre-checks — key injection, connectivity, baseline health checks (3x simple inference at low QPS). Collector: Prometheus pushgateway on redwood-perf-collect.
- 22:00–22:10 UTC: cold-run (no cache priming), sample 600 requests at 10 RPS. Capture TTFT cold baseline.
- 22:10–22:40 UTC: warmup + steady-state run. Warmup = 5 mins ramp to 1800 RPS; steady-state = 25 mins at target concurrency. Collect P50/P95/P99 latencies and per-token throughput.
- 22:40–23:00 UTC: spike tests — short bursts to 320 concurrency and 3x token length.
- Post-run: immediate upload of raw traces + completion note to this thread.

Laura: please confirm Prometheus scrape targets and Grafana dashboard share. Aditya: orchestration timeline (k8s jobs + load generator) and retry policy if we see transient auth token rotation.

Karthik
From: DataCo Performance Team <perf@dataco.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@dataco.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 23:45:12 +0000
Subject: Re: MAP + performance runbook and access (DataCo) — run 1 summary

Karthik / team — quick summary from tonight's window. Raw CSV attached (run_summary_0915.csv). Top-line:

- Peak concurrency seen: 320 at 22:46 UTC.
- Steady-state throughput: median 1,950 RPS during the 25-minute window.
- Median TTFT: 85 ms (warm-cache).
- P95 latency: 420 ms; P99 latency: 1,200 ms during a single 2-minute blip between 23:12–23:14 (auth token refresh caused ~2 min elevated p99).
- Observability: Prometheus scrape gaps noted at 23:11–23:13 (collector restart). Screenshots attached (run-screenshots-0915.png).

Request: can Redwood re-run a targeted 30-minute steady-state only (no spikes) to validate P95 without the collector restart interfering? Also include a run with 4x token length median to evaluate kernel selection impact.

Attachments: run_summary_0915.csv, run-screenshots-0915.png

— DataCo Performance Team
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@dataco.com>, DataCo Performance Team <perf@dataco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 11:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MAP + performance runbook and access (DataCo) — final notes and next steps

Thanks for the detailed run and the artifacts. Summary from Redwood side and next steps:

- What passed: steady-state throughput (1,950 RPS) and median TTFT (85ms) meet or exceed the success thresholds in the MAP. Peak concurrency was within expected headroom.
- What failed / needs follow-up: P95 is 420ms which is within the MAP threshold but the P99 blip tied to the auth token refresh and collector restart is a concern. We propose a clean 30-minute steady-state re-run (no spikes) with extended scraping redundancy to rule out collector-side gaps.
- Action items and owners:
  - Redwood (Aditya): schedule re-run Sep 19 00:00–00:30 UTC, ensure load generator seeds 4x token-length profile.
  - DataCo (Dana): provide short-lived KMS token valid for Sep 19 and confirm collector retry policy won't evict metrics.
  - Laura: aggregate traces and produce a short-side-by-side comparison report for the MAP (deliverable due Sep 21). Report file will be final-map-results-20260917.pdf.

We can also discuss a one-time account credit for the overtime window as a closing concession; happy to include that in the MAP handoff.

Final attachments: final-map-results-20260917.pdf (summary + recommended mitigation steps).

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
